gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi reads deep through the middle, with rounded forms left unsealed at the edges. Noto Sans Yi sits under Styro's crowded, retro lettering and lets the heading's tight, closed shapes stand out by comparison.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squa: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square has a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square is the open one here, while Styro's retro, crowded letters stay shut tight, and that clash is the pair's best quality.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Retro punch, then a softer follow-up. Styro crowds its letters into a commanding block, so if it were made small the tight shapes would clog, while Noto Traditional Nushu with its broad-nibbed, open stroke would hold up when enlarged.
gen-fs-styro-gf-numans: Styro packs its retro lowercase so tight that the letters nearly touch. Numans answers by hanging the ends of its s far from the spine and spreading its coiled-rope letters wide, which makes the closed-versus-open difference the pair's best quality.
gen-fs-styro-gf-onest: Retro and crowded up top, then Onest with big bowls and short ascenders below. Styro's closed shapes meet Onest's open curves.
gen-fs-styro-gf-puritan: Commanding is Styro's mood, with retro letters pressed close and shut. But Puritan opens its rounded forms and oversized e and a counters, so the two sit together as a tight shout and a wide-open reply.
gen-fs-styro-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big reads like a monoline sans-serif, its terminals finishing clear of the stem and its x-height filling the line. Radio Canada Big would carry a long passage easily, a steady, open counterpoint to Styro's crowded retro display letters.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sarpanch: Styro is retro, commanding and packed tight. Sarpanch brings a clearly open lowercase e and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, so the heading's shut-in letters get an easy, approachable partner.
gen-fs-styro-gf-stack-sans-notch: Styro is crowded, retro and commanding. It excels at making a loud entrance, while Stack Sans Notch, with open curves you can see into and rod-stock lines, is built for quiet, big-bodied lowercase words.
gen-fs-styro-gf-stack-sans-text: Commanding describes Styro, whose retro lowercase is pressed tight and closed. And Stack Sans Text counters with a marker-like constant line and curve endings kept well apart, so it handles the reading while Styro handles the announcing.
